The shift in market sentiment follows renewed inflation concerns linked to the AI-driven rally, prompting traders to adjust their interest rate forecasts. According to Yahoo Finance, there is now a 95% probability that the Federal Reserve will implement a 25 basis point rate hike in December, with a 5% chance of a 50 basis point increase. Meanwhile, oil prices have retreated by approximately 1%.

Looking ahead to the upcoming Thanksgiving and Black Friday period, market participants are monitoring a wave of corporate earnings reports. article.headline: Jack Edwards clinches thriller as Australia overcomes England in T20 series opener
article.summary: Australia secured a tense final-over victory against England at the Melbourne Cricket Ground to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.
article.body:
Nikhil Chaudhary delivered a standout performance, hitting 66 runs and taking 2-21 to help Australia chase down a target of 191 with three wickets and just one ball remaining. This result marks the highest successful T20 chase for Australia on home soil, proving vital as the team fields a host of new faces to move past recent off-field controversies.

For cricket fans, this opening match signals a shift in momentum toward the series newcomers. The game was marked by high tension and on-field exchanges, particularly involving Chaudhary during his match-defining knock. The atmosphere turned electric at the Melbourne Cricket Ground as the crowd reacted to England's attempts to slow the pace in the closing moments of the game.

England set a competitive total of 187-9, fueled by Harry Brook’s aggressive 65 off 28 balls. Despite England’s efforts to defend 11 runs in the final over, Jack Edwards remained composed to finish 25 not out and seal the win. The performance of Chaudhary, who moved from Delhi to Brisbane, provided the necessary spark to counter the early loss of opener Jake Fraser-McGurk.

With Australia holding a 1-0 series lead, the pressure now shifts to the second match of the series. England will look to level the contest when the two teams meet again on the Gold Coast this Tuesday.

article.headline: Level 4 thunderstorm warning triggers emergency standby across KwaZulu-Natal province today
article.summary: Emergency teams are on high alert in KwaZulu-Natal as authorities issue a yellow level 4 weather warning for heavy rain, damaging winds, and hail.
article.body:
Disaster management teams across the province are preparing for impact as forecasts signal a period of severe instability across northern and central districts. Officials have explicitly advised residents in low-lying areas and informal settlements to seek immediate shelter and strictly avoid flood-prone zones to prevent further devastation caused by ongoing heavy downpours. The threat to local infrastructure and daily movement remains high as these systems move through the region.

This alert carries significant risk for motorists and residents alike, as the threat includes severe lightning and flash flooding capable of disrupting essential services. Following established safety protocols is essential, particularly for those in vulnerable communities, as authorities warn that previous rainfall events have already destabilized various parts of the province. Emergency personnel have been positioned to respond to potential incidents caused by these extreme conditions.

According to the South African Weather Service, the yellow level 4 warning encompasses multiple regions, with eThekwini Municipality confirming that emergency teams are on standby for both Monday and Tuesday. Communities specifically identified as being at risk include KwaMashu, Inanda, uMlazi, Chatsworth, Phoenix, and Pinetown. Cooperative Governance spokesperson Siboniso Mngadi and MEC Thulasizwe Buthelezi have both urged the public to exercise extreme caution when navigating roads, specifically warning against the attempt to cross flooded bridges or water-covered surfaces. As the situation develops, citizens are encouraged to monitor updates and prioritize safety by avoiding unnecessary travel until the severe weather conditions subside.

article.summary: Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho makes six lineup changes for the Champions League clash against PSV, including resting Jude Bellingham.
article.body:
Real Madrid head coach Jose Mourinho is rotating his squad heavily for tonight’s Champions League match, as Jude Bellingham moves to the bench to accommodate six changes from the team's last appearance. The decision follows Mourinho’s prior warning regarding the heavy schedule, which sees the squad playing three matches within an eight-day window.

This shift in strategy highlights the internal squad management required as Madrid navigates a packed European and domestic calendar. With Vinícius Jr. returning to the starting eleven, the tactical setup shifts significantly, placing Arda Güler in the '10' role, with Diomande on the right and Vinícius operating on the left to support Kylian Mbappé.

The starting defensive line features Valverde and Cucurella as full-backs, with Militao and Rüdiger anchoring the center, while Bernardo and Tchouaméni form the double pivot. Courtois remains the confirmed starter in goal for the encounter at the Santiago Bernabéu.

Opponents PSV Eindhoven arrive with their own tactical adjustment, as coach Peter Bosz brings in 20-year-old Paul Wanner to replace Mauro Júnior, who faces a long-term injury layoff until the end of the year. article.headline: Al Ahly Sacks Hussein Amouta After Defeat Ends 14-Match Unbeaten Streak
article.summary: Egyptian giants Al Ahly dismissed head coach Hussein Amouta and his staff on Tuesday following a 2-0 loss to Pyramids.
article.body:
The 2-0 defeat against Pyramids in the ninth round of the Egyptian Premier League served as the final straw, snapping Hussein Amouta’s 14-match unbeaten run across all competitions. Before this loss, the coach had secured 11 wins and two draws since taking the helm in mid-June. According to Goal.com, the club confirmed the dismissal in an official statement released early Tuesday morning, effectively ending his tenure alongside his backroom staff.

This leadership change directly impacts the club’s trajectory for the remainder of the season, as management moves to stabilize the first team. The decision followed an assessment by vice-president Yassin Mansour and board member Sayed Abdel Hafiz, who now lead the search for a successor. Broadcaster Ahmed Shobeir suggested that the club’s management is under pressure to avoid rushing the appointment, emphasizing the need to address structural issues within the football department rather than just focusing on immediate results. In response to the poor form, the club has also implemented a freeze on player payments.

The search for a new head coach is already underway, with the board expected to review candidates in the coming hours. While broadcaster Ibrahim Fayek reported that the club is leaning toward an Egyptian appointment with four names currently under consideration, ON Sport noted that former assistant Sami Qamsan is the most prominent candidate on the list. The final decision remains subject to the club’s ability to secure a strong foreign coach who meets their current strategic requirements.

Following the exit of the Moroccan coach, the board must navigate a challenging transition period. As reported by Shobeir, internal debates regarding the direction of the club's coaching appointments have persisted, including past disagreements over the choice of leadership.

article.headline: Brentford Routs Everton 4-0 as Tarkowski Sees First Career Red Card
article.summary: Brentford climbed to sixth in the Premier League table after a 4-0 win against Everton, marked by Keane Lewis-Potter’s double and a contentious red card for James Tarkowski.
article.body:
James Tarkowski’s dismissal at the Gtech Community Stadium ended a remarkable Premier League record; the Everton captain had avoided a red card in all 350 of his previous appearances. His first-ever red card occurred after a VAR review upgraded a yellow card for a follow-through challenge on Yehor Yarmoliuk, with officials citing high studs and significant force. The sending-off leaves Tarkowski suspended for Sunday’s upcoming Merseyside derby.

The 4-0 defeat represents the heaviest loss for Everton since David Moyes returned to the club at the start of last year. For Moyes, the night was particularly difficult as it marked his 593rd game as Everton manager, setting a new club record for the most matches in charge, yet the result saw his side drop to ninth in the standings.

Keane Lewis-Potter secured the victory for the hosts with two deflected strikes within four minutes during the first half. Vitaly Janelt added a third goal with a 25-yard rocket in the 67th minute, and substitute Fabio Carvalho scored a fourth in stoppage time to complete the rout. According to the Premier League match centre, the referee ultimately ruled that Tarkowski’s challenge endangered the safety of his opponent.

Brentford now sits in sixth place, one point ahead of Everton. Moyes will look to recover in his next outing, while Brentford prepares to maintain their position in the league following this comprehensive performance.

article.headline: Tape found in bin sparked suspicion during 2018 sandpaper ball tampering scandal
article.summary: Evidence of tape containing super glue and grit led to suspicions of ball tampering by David Warner during the 2018 Cape Town series.
article.body:
An ICC representative attempted to test discarded finger and thumb strapping on David Warner’s digits to see if it fit, in a scene described as worthy of the OJ trial. According to reports from SEN’s Gerard Whateley, the strapping was recovered from the field by grounds staff and handed to officials, with an ICC source later claiming it contained a mixture of super glue and grit. Warner was the primary focus of South African networks at the time, as Cameron Bancroft later noted in a 4,497-word column that Warner was the brains behind the tampering plot but felt he could not personally carry it out due to camera scrutiny.

The revelations highlight the intense friction within the Australian squad as the scandal unfolded. At the team hotel, a heated confrontation occurred between Warner and Mitch Marsh. Sources described the scene as one where Cameron Bancroft attempted to take responsibility, Steve Smith sought to mediate, and Warner remained largely detached while walking the corridors. The incident was part of a broader atmosphere of denial and finger-pointing that divided Cricket Australia’s players and staff.

Even after the events in Cape Town, the habit of ball manipulation proved difficult to abandon. Gerard Whateley revealed that during the 2018 series against Pakistan, a player asked, “Who’s got the mints?” while searching for ways to take wickets on a flat Dubai pitch. The comment was met with a sharp rebuke from a teammate who insisted the squad would not repeat their previous mistakes. Captain Tim Paine and coach Justin Langer ultimately intervened to stop a substitute fielder from bringing items onto the field, maintaining a strict team policy against having lollies on the pitch to avoid any negative perception.
